title: Tenant locality assertion engine and evidence catalog for Hosted API
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise tenants need an auditable, tamper-evident way to assert and demonstrate where their request data was processed by the Hosted API. Current controls only allow coarse "preferred region" hints and ad-hoc evidence exports.

Goal: Implement a Tenant Locality Assertion Engine (TLAE) that (1) enforces pinning policies at request-time, (2) emits structured, queryable evidence records for every routed request, and (3) provides a downloadable evidence catalog for auditors with configurable retention windows.

Out of scope: Private/VPC hosted control plane; on-prem deployment automation; long-term cold archival (>2 years) for now.

Design summary: 
- Policy DSL: extend existing residency policy language to support pin priority, soft-fallback windows, and per-tenant retention overrides.
- Enforcement: routing layer will consult TLAE before dispatching. If policy violation occurs, either block request or route to approved fallback model/region as per tenant policy.
- Evidence records: per-request JSON lines containing tenant_id, request_id, timestamp, resolved_region, resolved_zone, model_variant, route_decision_reason, policy_version, and a cryptographic signature (HMAC) signed by the control plane key to prevent tampering.
- Evidence catalog: a time-bounded index providing (a) per-tenant manifest for requested window, (b) batch export API and signed bundle package (tar+manifest+signatures), and (c) retention controls surfaced in Console and API.

API/Console changes: 
- API: new endpoints POST /v1/tenants/{id}/residency-policy (CRUD), GET /v1/tenants/{id}/evidence?start=&end=, POST /v1/tenants/{id}/evidence/export
- Console: Residency policy editor (JSON + form), evidence export UX with preview and retention dropdown, and an audit tab showing recent policy violations and fallback events.

Telemetry & observability: emit events: residency.policy.eval, residency.route.decision, residency.evidence.export with structured tags to Console dashboards. Add sampling controls for high-volume tenants.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Policy DSL implemented and documented in spec.
2) Routing consults TLAE in 99.95% of requests within 50ms policy lookup latency under normal load.
3) Evidence records are generated and verifiable via HMAC; export bundles can be generated and downloaded from Console.
4) Per-tenant retention setting enforces expiry (TTL) on evidence manifested in S3 lifecycle + control-plane index.
5) End-to-end integration test and security review completed.

Security & compliance: HSM/KMS integration for signing keys required in Private mode; for Hosted API we use control-plane KMS with strict key rotation policies. Data in evidence bundles must exclude raw request payloads unless tenant explicitly opts-in.

Open questions / tradeoffs: 
- Signed evidence format vs. append-only audit logs: chose signed per-request records to keep exports portable for customers.
- Granularity of retained metadata: store routing metadata by default, keep raw prompts only if tenant enables "full audit" (opt-in).
- Cost: retention beyond 90 days increases storage costs; propose default 30/90/365 tiers.

Stakeholders: PM Asha Patel, Eng leads: Miguel Santos (routing), Lena Brunner (console), Security: Ethan Cho.
comments: 2026-03-02 | Miguel Santos: Initial alignment meeting — agreed on signed evidence approach. Action: middleware prototype by 2026-03-09.
2026-03-05 | Lena Brunner: Console mockups reviewed; suggested adding 'preview' before export and clearer retention lables. Filing DES follow-up.
2026-03-09 | Miguel Santos: Middleware prototype implemented; policy lookup cached in-memory with invalidation TTL=30s. Found race when policy updates coincide with requests; added locking.
2026-03-11 | Security (Ethan Cho): Requested KMS usage for signing and a threat model doc. Also asked to exclude raw prompt content by default.
2026-03-12 | Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include export package signature and retention enforcement tests.
qa_plan: Unit tests for DSL parser, integration tests for routing decision paths, e2e test for export bundle generation and signature verification, and a canary run with 2 pilot tenants for 2 weeks. QA checklist will be attached to PR.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal canary (routing-only) + console disabled for tenants. Phase 2: opt-in tenants can enable evidence exports. Phase 3: default availability with tiered retention after two weeks and customer communications. Use feature flag residenty.tlae.enable.
